subject: Data retention & purge timeline — logs, backups, prompt data

Subject: Data retention & purge timeline — logs, backups, prompt data

Hi Diana,

Thanks for sending the security questionnaire. I pulled the retention items into a short summary to answer the OptimaBank questions about logs, backups, prompt retention, and purge timelines. Please find an attached one-page summary (redwood-data-retention-2026-03.pdf) and a draft DPA for reference.

Quick summary: 
- Application logs (auth / request / routing): retained 90 days by default; aggregated metrics retained 2 years.
- Access/audit logs (admin actions, key changes): retained 365 days for audit purposes.
- Backups (model & data snapshots): rolling backups retained for 30 days; immutable snapshots for critical system state retained up to 90 days on request (subject to support/contract).
- Prompt/request payloads (customer request bodies): default retention 30 days for quality/regression detection; opt-in configurable retention windows available for Dedicated/Private deployments.
- Prompt purge SLA: we can perform account-level prompt deletions within 72 hours after verification of request for hosted accounts (private deployments have different procedures documented in the DPA).
- Deletion notes: deletion removes live records and search/index metadata; immutable backup snapshots may require additional retention steps and are purged on a 30-day cycle unless otherwise agreed.

I attached the one-pager and the DPA draft. Let me know if you want more granular timelines (per-log-type) or an audit/export showing purge events.

Thanks,
Marissa

Hi team,

Answers to the technical items below: 
1) Purge request verification: For hosted accounts we require an authenticated request via the account owner or an admin with MFA-enabled console access. Deletions initiated by Support require a signed ticket and explicit written authorization (email or DocuSign) from the designated account admin; we log the action and include the support ticket ID in the audit trail.

2) Backups and encryption: All backups are encrypted at rest using customer-managed KMS keys when customers provide them (default is Redwood-managed KMS). Backups are versioned and stored in immutable object storage with a 30-day rolling retention period. On contract termination, we can schedule destruction of backups and associated object storage within 30 days of verified termination, provided there are no outstanding legal holds. For immutable snapshots older than 30 days we can include a clause in the DPA to shorten the snapshot retention window to meet customer needs — this typically requires 30 days' lead time to coordinate storage provider lifecycle policies.

3) Scoped prompt deletion: We support scoped deletion by conversation ID, request ID, or time range for hosted customers. The deletion pipeline marks live records for removal, purges search/index metadata, and issues a delete job against our KV & blob storage. Status is reported back as a purge job with a unique job id; batch jobs can take up to 72 hours to fully complete across caches and asynchronous workers. We also produce a machine-readable report showing request IDs and records deleted (CSV) and an audit log entry per job.

Implementation caveats: immutable backups may contain copies of prompt payloads. If a customer needs immediate removal from backups, we recommend an expedited remediation run (extra fee possible) to identify and destroy specific snapshots; otherwise, the normal backup purge cycle applies.

Let me know if you want the exact API endpoints and sample curl commands for scoped purge jobs — I can add that to the one-pager.

– Dev

Hi Diana / Evan,

Following up with the legal and compliance side: 
- Verification / authorization: we will require the account admin to submit a purge request via the console or via a signed DocuSign (we can accept either). Support-initiated deletions are only executed with documented, auditable authorization and are logged.
- Evidence & reporting: we will provide a purge job report (CSV) plus an audit log extract (JSON/CSV) that shows the actor, timestamp, and job id. We can also provide a redacted screenshot of the console job for manual verification if needed.
- BAA / HIPAA: Redwood can sign a BAA for covered deployments; we recommend Dedicated or Private deployment for high-PHI workloads. The DPA draft attached contains HIPAA-specific addenda; legal is ready to discuss specific flow-level safeguards.
- SLA for purge confirmation: standard hosted SLA for purge completion is 72 hours after verified request; if Optima requires a shorter SLA we can include an accelerated purge clause in the DPA (subject to operational feasibility and potential billing for expedited snapshot processing).

I attached a suggested DPA paragraph for deletion & backup destruction to the shared DPA draft (see link). Happy to walk through it with your legal team.

Best,
